newsitem.title: USA: North American GSM phone cos form data alliance.
newsitem.headline: North American GSM phone cos form data alliance.

text.p: Wireless phone companies backing the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) standard said they formed an alliance designed to boost the system's use in mobile data as well as voice communications.

Seven U.S. and Canadian GSM-based personal communications services (PCS) providers formed the alliance. Intel Corp, the microprocessor giant, said it lent its support to the alliance in a bid to fuel wireless data market growth.
GSM is an international communications standard for wireless transmission of both voice and data. But, to date, GSM's data-handling capabilities have won few U.S. customers.

Using cellular networks to transmit computer data has become popular in Europe, where GSM is the dominant standard, but has been slow to take off in the United States, where wireless data standards have been slow to develop and remain expensive compared with alternative communication methods.

Members of the GSM Alliance include Aerial Communications Inc, BellSouth Corp's Mobility DCS unit, Microcell Telecommunications Inc., Omnipoint Corp's Communications unit, SBC Communications Inc's Pacific Bell Mobile Services, Powertel Inc and Western Wireless Corp.

Among the competing digital standards for wireless communications, GSM has won the most customers to date in the United States, according to Phillip Redman, a mobile communications analyst at Yankee Group.

Within the United States, GSM had signed up 646,000 subscribers as of the end of June, versus 420,000 for Code Division Multiple Access, a competing standard developed by Qualcomm Inc, according to Yankee Group estimates.
